## Purpose

Assess whether current delivery work and recent approved changes remain within the approved Option B scope boundary. Identify scope variance, traceability gaps, deferred work, and any proposed updates that require PM direction. This run does not accept deliverables, change the approved baseline, approve unrecorded scope, close control items, or replace the later PM-15 acceptance review.

## Scope Boundary

The review covers the approved Option B scope and requirements, the current product backlog, recent approved and proposed changes, the current local Session Materials and Q&A increment, and related delivery constraints. It preserves the approved exclusions, the local-only email-verification exception, the unresolved target-state access and participant-data conditions, and the SharePoint fallback.

## Tailoring Decision

| Factor | Project evidence | Effect on rigor |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | The application protects restricted participant content and is targeted for availability before 2026-09-11. | Scope variance and unapproved work must be visible before staging or launch decisions. |
| Scale | The team and product are small, but the MVP spans access, classroom, community, calendar, administration, security, and operations. | A focused traceability and variance review is sufficient; a new scope document is not assumed. |
| Duration | The remaining delivery window is short and the schedule is conditional. | Review recent changes and active work now; record concrete next triggers without inventing dates. |
| Complexity | Authentication, participant data, staging, operations, Q&A moderation, and launch gates affect the boundary. | Keep deferred, unresolved, and local-only conditions separate from completed scope. |
| Approach | Delivery is iterative from local implementation toward staging. | Compare the current increment with the approved baseline and backlog rather than treating local work as launch acceptance. |
| Governance | The requester and IT team own scope and priorities; the LeadLab Director gives final launch acceptance. | Propose, but do not approve, baseline or scope changes. |

## Minimum Output

1. Scope-variance review for recent approved changes and current delivery work.
2. Traceability check across the scope baseline, backlog, change log, decisions, and local build evidence.
3. Explicit treatment of approved, deferred, unresolved, and potentially unrecorded scope.
4. Proposed record or artifact updates, with PM-only decisions clearly separated.
5. Next trigger for the scope-control review and the later acceptance review.
